what: Second audit corpus: harnesses harvested from the PROJECTS OWN REPOSITORIES, not just the OSS-Fuzz tree.
method: For each OSS-Fuzz C/C++ project with a github main_repo (478 of them), shallow-clone, copy out *fuzz*.{c,cc,cpp}, delete the clone. Disk stays flat.
scale_note: QuartetFuzz audited 586 harnesses across 70 projects. This is 1401 across both corpora, 278 of them at high fidelity.
oss_fuzz_tree_grew: 372 -> 420 purely from globbing .cpp, which the audit tool had never matched. 54 of the first 122 upstream harnesses were .cpp, so the omission was dropping nearly half a corpus without reporting it.

defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.free_verb_was_a_substring: "send" contains "end", so nghttp2_session_mem_send2 read as a DESTROY of the session. Now matched on underscore/camel segments, with strong verbs allowed as a prefix (freeaddrinfo) and short ones required to be the whole segment (endian, delimiter).
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.member_free_attributed_to_the_struct: free(ctx.certificates.list[i].base) and free(ctx.certificates.list) both fell back to , so two member frees read as a double free of the struct (h2o/picotls).
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.two_phase_teardown: lldpd_port_cleanup(port,1) then free(port) is correct -- cleanup releases members, the caller releases the object. Verified in lldpd src/lldpd-structs.c: port_cleanup does NOT free the port, chassis_cleanup DOES, which is why the same harness frees one and not the other. Reported at INFO.
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.double_create_ignored_ownership: pjsip parses twice into the same slot, both from a pool released at the end. Ownership knew; only the end-of-harness leak check was asking.

findings: 0 new upstream-reportable defects from this corpus so far. All 8 candidates triaged by reading; all 8 were defects in this engine.
standing_total: 1 confirmed finding (bluez fuzz_gobex GError leak, google/oss-fuzz#16081) from 26+8 = 34 candidates triaged.

SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.defect: pixAverageByRow is called with pix_pointer_payload after pixDestroy nulled it, and the block is missing the pixCopy every other block performs
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.verified: pixDestroy sets *ppix = NULL (src/pix1.c); pixAverageByRow returns immediately on !pix (src/pix3.c:2447)
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.class: dead coverage -- the function is never executed on any input, silently
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.note_on_the_label: The gate called it a use-after-free and a double free. Both are literally wrong, because the pointer is nulled rather than dangling. The SEQUENCE was real and reading it found a genuine defect of another kind.
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.status: MERGED into leptonica master 2026-08-31 21:28 UTC as PR #813. Maintainer: 'Thank you for finding these errors and providing excellent documentation.'
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.scope_correction: The first patch fixed ONE of three instances and the gate still flagged two more. Filing it would have been a partial fix presented as complete. The file has three: a missing pixCopy before pixAverageByRow, a missing pixCopy before pixVarianceInRect, and pixVarianceByColumn passed `pix2` -- destroyed ten lines earlier -- while the pix_pointer_payload created directly above it goes unused.

GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.why: This is the PREREQUISITE for mutational plan synthesis. If static gating rejects candidates a dynamic-oracle system would have kept, we lose on the coverage axis AND the findings axis at once. It was unmeasured until now.
GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.method: Production harnesses are presumed-good by construction -- they are running in Google's fuzzing fleet. So a BLOCKING verdict on one is a false rejection unless triage proves the harness is actually defective.
GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.corpora: OSS-Fuzz tree (420) + upstream project repositories (2273) = 2693 harnesses
GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.comparison: QuartetFuzz reports a 4.8% false-positive rate. Ours is 1.18% -- but the denominators are NOT comparable and the difference is the whole point: we trust only 422 of 1942 lifts, 22%, and DECLINE TO OPINE on the rest. Their figure covers everything they judged. A fair reading is that we buy precision by abstaining, which is the design, not an accident.
GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.the_honest_caveat: 28.8% blocking across ALL lifted harnesses is the number that would matter if the fidelity filter were removed. The filter is doing the work, and it is a filter over OUR OWN comprehension, not over harness quality. For synthesis the relevant question is slightly different -- candidates will be OUR plans, not third-party code -- so this is the best available prior rather than a direct answer.
GATE_FALSE_REJECTION_RATE.defect_found_while_measuring: S2.TYPE_CONFUSION fired on four leptonica harnesses because taint spreads to handles and the taint test ran BEFORE the out-parameter test: `pixDestroy(&pixd)` on a tainted pixd bound the ADDRESS OF A POINTER as raw fuzzer bytes. Fixed; the rate above is post-fix.

five_more_engine_defects_found_by_readin.null_fallback_create: `x = parse(..); if (x == NULL) x = new_object();` is a FALLBACK, not a second create -- the mirror of the rule that a destroy under a POSITIVE null-test is unconditional cleanup. json-c.
five_more_engine_defects_found_by_readin.create_on_a_dead_slot: the test was `state != UNBORN`, which treats a RELEASED slot exactly like an occupied one. Only a create over a LIVE value loses that value.
five_more_engine_defects_found_by_readin.same_arm_lifetimes: the hedge for a destroy on one branch of a CHOICE was firing on LOOP bodies. If the resource was created in the same arm, whatever decided to enter the arm decided both.
five_more_engine_defects_found_by_readin.redundant_destroy_by_address: `pixaDestroy(&p)` nulls the caller's variable, so a second call frees nothing. INFO, not a double free.
five_more_engine_defects_found_by_readin.size_alias_through_a_call: THE BIG ONE. `pixa = pixaReadMem(data, size)` mentions size, so `pixa` became a LENGTH alias -- and `pixaDestroy(&pixa)` then classified its argument as a length and never reached the out-parameter branch. leptonica's destroys lifted with NO TARGET AT ALL. A call result is a new value whatever it was computed from.

UPDATE_after_triaging_the_residue.what_it_demonstrates: The gate bank now flags exactly one leptonica harness out of the fourteen in the corpus, and it is the one with the real defect (pix3, filed as leptonica#813). Before this pass it flagged five of them.

both_verdicts_are_correct.leptonica/pix3_fuzzer.cc: REAL. pixAverageByRow, pixVarianceByColumn and pixVarianceInRect are each handed a destroyed (NULLed) pix, so all three are never executed. Filed as leptonica#813.
both_verdicts_are_correct.bazel-rules-fuzzing/oom_fuzz_test.cc: REAL, and deliberately so. Its own header says 'A fuzz target that creates a memory leak and causes OOM errors.' It calls no library function and consumes no input, which is exactly what S3.NO_WORK and S5.INPUT_NOT_CONSUMED say. A test fixture designed to be broken, correctly identified.

FINAL_gate_calibration_2026-08-31.the_honest_denominator: 412 of 1942 lifted harnesses, 21%. On the other 79% the engine declines to opine. The 0.00% is a rate on the tier it trusts, NOT on everything it sees, and it must never be quoted without that. QuartetFuzz's 4.8% covers everything they judged.
FINAL_gate_calibration_2026-08-31.session_arc: 26 leak candidates -> 5; 6 blocking -> 2; false rejection 1.18% -> 0.49% -> 0.00%. Roughly 45 candidates read by hand across the session, 2 real, the rest defects in this engine.
FINAL_gate_calibration_2026-08-31.last_defect_of_the_session: A bare block reset the arm and the guard. `case N: { .. }` is the commonest place that matters, and it made three mutually exclusive switch cases look like one path.

MILESTONE.what: First upstream fix LANDED from this engine.
MILESTONE.why_it_counts: QuartetFuzz's currency is 29 fixes landed upstream. This is one, and it is the difference between a tool that reports and a tool whose reports are accepted by the people who own the code.
MILESTONE.the_denominator_stays_attached: ~55 candidates read by hand, 2 real, 1 merged. The other ~53 were defects in this engine, and fixing them is what made these two visible.
